Comparison Summary DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Max) is amongst the leading models in intelligence and reasonably priced when comparing to other open weight models of similar size. It's also notably fast, however very verbose. The model supports text and image input, outputs text, and has a 1M tokens context window.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Max) scores 45 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it well above average among comparable models (median: 19). When evaluating the Intelligence Index, it generated 210M tokens, which is very verbose in comparison to the median of 140M.

Pricing for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Max) is $0.30 per 1M input tokens (moderately priced, median: $0.43) and $1.20 per 1M output tokens (moderately priced, median: $1.68). On average, it costs $0.26 per task to evaluate DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Max) on the Intelligence Index.

At 225 tokens per second, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Max) is notably fast (78).

reactions: [Hacker News] I ran the Strata project with this on 32gb ram 16gb AMD 7900XTX. It goes about 20tok/s off the ssd. I'm guessing 64gb would go to 40tok/s. https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata Quality wise its not fast enough for me to eval. I'll probably spend some tokens on it through openrouter. DeepSeek 4 flash though is a mess compared to GPT Sol 6.1.

[Hacker News] I can believe it. Using DS4.1 to decomp old games, it is quite capable of doing so, but the amount of mistakes it makes, by the time I get it right Sol 6.1 would have long ported it correctly more thoroughly. For some tasks Sol really shows its superiority
[Hacker News] talking about "my setup" should require the good-old-days post footer that includes hardware details.
[Hacker News] There is so much down pressure, I cannot imagine the token/s price going up. It has been going down and will continue doing so, we are far from a plateau IMHO

[Hacker News] I'm running it at 3 b.p.w. and it really feels better than Flash 4 at 4 b.p.w. for me. Some of these EXL3 calibrated quants are like magic. It also has 196B ngram params that sit on disk. So it's really pretty comparable to GLM 5.3 in size.

[Hacker News] Everything's been trending down so far, so until evidence shows otherwise, I'd assume it will continue that trend. IMO the best time to buy local infra will be when that trend begins to asymptote.
